title: Coal and energy workers’ protest outside the National Assembly
location: In front of the National Assembly, Sofia
organizer: KNSB/CITUB, Confederation of Labour Podkrepa, and affiliated energy/mining-sector unions
participants_original: KNSB and NOVA each report more than 3,000 workers; NOVA does not state its count source.
threshold_50_evidence: The organizer KNSB and contemporaneous broadcaster NOVA each report over 3,000 workers. The estimate origin is not independently documented; the conservative lower bound still exceeds 50.

start_date.summary: Both contemporaneous reports identify the protest as occurring on 12 January 2023.

end_date.summary: Neither article establishes when the physical assembly ended.

location.summary: Both place the workers outside the National Assembly in Sofia.

scope.summary: The unions describe workers from coal/thermal-energy employers across Bulgaria at a national-policy protest in the capital.

organizer.summary: KNSB and Podkrepa are identified with the action; NOVA says unions organized it.

demands.summary: Textual demands concern renegotiating the Recovery and Resilience Plan energy chapter, removing its 40% emissions-reduction commitment and keeping coal plants operating through at least 2038. These do not map cleanly to the seven listed demand categories, so the category array is empty.

participants_original.summary: KNSB and NOVA both report more than 3,000; the organizer is a primary but interested source, and NOVA does not disclose a separate counting basis.

participants_min.summary: A conservative reported lower bound of 3,000 is directly supported by both “more than 3,000” reports; no upper bound is available.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both reports place the event well above 50, though the count source may not be independent.

protester_violence.summary: The read article prose does not establish protester violence or explicitly state that none occurred; value remains unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: KNSB says parliamentary-group representatives addressed the crowd at protesters’ request; NOVA says MPs from several groups joined and expressed support. This is coded as accommodation/contact, not as proof that the protest caused the formal vote or that demands were fully met.

state_response.arrests.summary: Neither read article reports event-specific arrests; silence is not coded as no_explicit.

state_response.beatings.summary: Neither read article reports event-specific beatings; value remains unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Neither read article establishes crowd dispersal; value remains unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: The sources report parliamentary contact but do not establish whether other government actors ignored the event; value remains unknown.

state_response.killings.summary: No event-specific killing evidence is reported; silence is not coded as no_explicit.

state_response.shootings.summary: No event-specific shooting evidence is reported; value remains unknown.

notes.summary: Specific energy-policy demands are kept in prose because they do not fit the listed categories. KNSB mentions a separate 11 November 2022 action over the same issue; this January assembly is a new physical event, not a January continuation of that earlier action.

notes: The demand categories available in the working protocol do not include these specific energy-transition/recovery-plan demands; the categories remain empty and textual goals are retained. The formal parliamentary resolution is documented in a partial BTA excerpt, but BTA does not describe the protest; no causal link between the vote and assembly is asserted. KNSB mentions a distinct 11 November 2022 action, not an ongoing physical episode.
open_questions: When did the assembly physically end?
What was the source/method behind the two >3,000 estimates, and were they independent?
Did parliamentary statements or the formal resolution represent a response to the protest, or only a same-day policy action?
How does the unavailable official codebook classify this energy-policy demand?

title: Reported Kustendil protest against increased municipal taxes and waste fees
location: Outside the Kustendil Municipality building (announced venue; execution unverified)
participants_original: A search-only Lupa result says several hundred residents protested; no source body confirms the count.
threshold_50_evidence: A search-only Lupa result uses a several-hundred description, but the article body was not obtained. The body-read BNR source is only an advance notice. Threshold remains unverified.

start_date.summary: Three search-only reports identify a 16 January protest; the opened BNR report was a same-day announcement of a planned 16:30 event, not proof it occurred.

location.summary: Search leads and the BNR announcement place the planned protest at Kustendil Municipality; event execution and exact site remain unconfirmed.

scope.summary: The reported issue is a municipal tax and waste-fee increase in Kustendil.

organizer.summary: Organizer remains unknown. The mayor alleged that BSP and allied parties organized the planned protest; this is an unverified attributed allegation, not a confirmed organizer.

demands.summary: The search leads describe opposition to higher local taxes; the opened BNR announcement identifies vehicle/property-tax and waste-fee increases.

participants_original.summary: Only a search-result snippet says several hundred; it was not body-read or independently corroborated.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Several hundred appears only in a search snippet; the body-read BNR page announces a future event but does not report attendance.

protester_violence.summary: The advance notice does not report event violence and cannot establish whether the protest occurred; value unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: The mayor commented on the planned action before its scheduled start; no response to an executed assembly is established.

notes.summary: Kustendil.info, Focus and Lupa body opens returned Cache miss; a fresh-receipt ordinary HTTPS attempt to the exact Kustendil.info URL failed DNS before HTTP. The only opened body is a pre-event notice. A separate headline claims a mayor-resignation demand, not corroborated in the opened notice.

notes: Retain as a search-derived lead, not a verified occurrence: local outlets’ search results describe an actual 16 January protest, while the only body-read local public-radio page was published at 12:45 announcing a future 16:30 demonstration. The mayor alleged partisan organization; the allegation is not verified. The headline also mentions a mayor-resignation demand, which the opened notice does not confirm.
open_questions: Did the scheduled assembly actually take place?
Can an accessible contemporaneous report verify a count of at least 50?
Who organized it, and was the mayor-resignation demand made by participants?
What was the physical end time and any event-specific response?

title: Reported second Kustendil protest against local tax increases
participants_original: Search-only Struma headline characterizes a tax protest before a municipal-council session as low-turnout; no numeric count or opened report is available.
threshold_50_evidence: The only captured turnout description is the search-only Struma headline “low-turnout”; it does not establish whether 50 people attended. Pending body-level attendance evidence.

start_date.summary: The search result for Kustendil.info identifies this as a second protest on 26 January; the article body was not obtained.

location.summary: Search leads place a second tax protest in Kustendil; the precise venue is not verified for this date.

scope.summary: All captured leads concern Kustendil municipal taxes; exact demands and participation remain body-unverified.

demands.summary: Captured titles/metadata connect the leads to increased local taxes and a planned municipal-council session.

participants_original.summary: Search-only Struma title labels turnout low without a number.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The second-protest and BNR titles indicate a Kustendil action; the only turnout wording is the un-opened Struma headline “low-turnout,” insufficient to decide the 50-person threshold.

notes.summary: Keep this reported 26 January action separate from the reported 16 January rally. A shared episode key marks only a tentative campaign relationship; the date boundary, distinct execution and continuity are not confirmed by body-level evidence.

notes: A captured Kustendil.info search result calls this a second protest on 26 January; BNR and Struma search leads also concern Kustendil tax protest activity. All corresponding body attempts returned Cache miss before HTTP; the exact Kustendil.info/BNR domains also failed DNS on ordinary HTTPS attempts. Do not infer under-50 attendance from “low turnout.” The episode key is tentative and does not merge this with BG202301-E002.
open_questions: Did a separate physical action take place on 26 January?
What was the exact site and attendee count?
Did it belong to the same tax campaign as BG202301-E002, and was there an ongoing assembly or a separate day of action?
